name: Question 10
problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=6-4x$ and $y=2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-x & \,⟹\,x=-y \\ y=6-4x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4} \\ y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/08237d1ca2e01d0cf620dfa06a4265d8053b7ee34d0b65036aad7d5734726e1c.png)

 

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/c756dc7924fc4c116601da907eb3b767b8a40647e063c146dad83b0ea660933b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-y\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-y}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=−x, y=6−4x and y=2x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫−20∫3/2−y/4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫−20∫6−4y−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫2y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy
c
∫−20∫−y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫2y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫3/2−y/4y/2f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows: y=−x⟹x=−yy=6−4x⟹x=32−y4y=2x⟹x=y2

Now, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−2≤y≤0,−y≤x≤32−y4} and D2={(x,y):0≤y≤2,y2≤x≤32−y4}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy.
